answer: For agents predicting ember spread or dune movement, assign a different hidden test case to every identity at each public randomness pulse. Require a signed commitment before revealing the scoring data; pay only for results that independent reviewers can reproduce. One correct answer cannot ripple across a swarm because each alias faces a distinct case. An attacker must fund separate computation and risk unpaid failures for every identity. This raises marginal cost rather than proving uniqueness; leaked test data or colluding reviewers can still defeat it.
